sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk rises as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
Its effect is strongest at high utilization, where the data show a sharp step up in risk at about 0.72.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver, and having any delinquency raises the risk of default compared with having none.
Annual income is also among the top few drivers, and higher income generally lowers the risk of default.
Length of credit history has at most a weak effect, with longer histories associated with slightly lower risk.
The data do not settle whether debt-to-income ratio affects risk, and age, the two standardised application attributes and credit inquiries hardly matter.
The effect of utilization is larger when delinquencies are present, while utilization and credit history do not interact in a way the data can detect.
